Rest in style and comfort

Haven blends luxury with warmth, genuine personalization and social life. Flexible, never casual.

The hotel comes close to its guests, on its own terms. 360° Rooftop & Restaurant, events and a direct connection with the city, always held to the same standard. The result: a stay that feels made for you, and unmistakably Haven.

Unforgettable moments

The location

Everything is walkable

Move the circle and see how much of El Poblado is within reach without getting into a car.

10 min

Drag to move · pinch to zoom

  1. A historic house devoted to salsa: around a hundred classic cocktails, Caribbean cooking and live orchestras at weekends.

    Directions ↗

  2. Medellín's modern classic: chef-driven cooking celebrating Colombian biodiversity in an intimate garden setting, steps from the hotel.

    Directions ↗

  3. No. 39 on The World's 50 Best Bars 2026: cocktails built on Afro-Colombian spirits and Andean herbs, in a conservatory courtyard.

    Directions ↗

  4. Grupo Carmen's tasting counter: a multi-course journey through ingredients from small Colombian growers.

    Directions ↗

  5. Grupo Carmen's polished steakhouse: dry-aged cuts, attentive service and a wine list built for red meat.

    Directions ↗

  6. Our 11th-floor terrace: heated pool, signature cocktails and the whole city around you. The best sunset in El Poblado.

    Directions ↗

  7. The lobby bar: specialty coffee in the morning and cocktails by night, to start or end the day without leaving.

    Directions ↗

  8. A curated concept store of fashion, jewellery, fragrance and homeware by leading Colombian designers.

    Directions ↗

  9. A terrace atop the Click Clack hotel with open valley views, signature cocktails and guest-chef pop-ups.

    Directions ↗

  10. A listening bar with a vinyl DJ at its centre, lava lamps and well-made classics: the ideal prelude to the night.

    Directions ↗

  11. Signature Colombian cooking from sea and grill, with fresh fish and a leafy, lantern-lit terrace in the heart of Provenza.

    Directions ↗

  12. Chef's counter devoted to ferments and strictly Colombian ingredients: an eight-course menu with cocktail or wine pairings.

    Directions ↗

  13. Beautifully plated brunch amid greenery, a couple of blocks from the Provenza bustle.

    Directions ↗

  14. A classic two-level rooftop with pool above The Charlee, mountain views and DJs; festive, with a dress code.

    Directions ↗

  15. Medellín debut of Celele's chef Jaime Rodríguez: a contemporary bistro built on Colombia's native pantry, opened mid-2026.

    Directions ↗

  16. Renzo Garibaldi's Lima butcher-grill arrives in Provenza: house dry-aged beef in a relaxed room.

    Directions ↗

  17. A shop of Colombian crafts and goods (coffee, sweets, textiles) steps from Provenza, with warm, personal service.

    Directions ↗

  18. Artisanal gelato built on Colombian fruits, with a queue that speaks for itself, two blocks from the hotel.

    Directions ↗

  19. The paisa institution for an honest bandeja paisa and mondongo soup, in generous portions with brisk service.

    Directions ↗

  20. A street-side Provenza bar with a DJ every night and bartenders who know their craft; an industry favourite after shift.

    Directions ↗

  21. Medellín's specialty-coffee benchmark: house roasting, direct ties to Antioquian farms and a leafy terrace on Vía Primavera.

    Directions ↗

  22. A disco speakeasy hidden behind a Japanese convenience-store façade, with experimental cocktails and weekly DJs.

    Directions ↗

  23. A bright indoor-outdoor space with a showpiece espresso machine and an all-morning menu made for lingering.

    Directions ↗

  24. Creative vegan cooking that wins over meat-eaters too: al pastor tacos, curry and crispy cauliflower on a leafy street.

    Directions ↗

  25. Contemporary art gallery circuit in Comuna 14 with coordinated openings; it starts almost next door to Haven.

    Directions ↗

  26. A boutique electronic club with top-tier sound and international DJs: El Poblado's reference for house and techno.

    Directions ↗

  27. A minimalist, intimate bar devoted to single-origin coffees, for those who put the cup ahead of brunch.

    Directions ↗

  28. A café-florist on a quiet street a few blocks from the hotel, with careful filter coffee and a generous brunch.

    Directions ↗

  29. A moody, tropical lounge-style interior with multiple brew methods: the most polished café for a date or meeting.

    Directions ↗

  30. Chef Jhon Zárate's local-produce bistro, on Latin America's 50 Best 2025 list. Small sharing plates on an ever-changing menu.

    Directions ↗

  31. White church opened in 1867 and rebuilt in the 1920s; altar and pulpit designed by Belgian architect Agustín Goovaerts.

    Directions ↗

  32. A bohemian dining room of plants and vintage books facing Parque El Poblado, serving creative Colombian sharing plates.

    Directions ↗

  33. A terrace by La Presidenta creek pouring craft beer and botanical cocktails alongside thin-crust vegetarian pizzas.

    Directions ↗

  34. An old house serving just three traditional soups: ajiaco, mondongo and beans. A simple, heartfelt Colombian lunch.

    Directions ↗

  35. An intimate wine bar, sibling to Sambombi, with a fine by-the-glass list and sharing plates by chef Jhon Zárate.

    Directions ↗

  36. Small-batch roaster in the heart of Manila, serving fresh, photogenic plates and hosting barista workshops.

    Directions ↗

  37. Square where San Lorenzo de Aburrá, the valley's first Spanish settlement, was founded in 1616; today a lively meeting point with crafts and cafés.

    Directions ↗

  38. Relaxed pan-Asian cooking, from ramen and bao to sushi, in a carefully designed space. Generous plates for sharing.

    Directions ↗

  39. Fully plant-based sushi and Japanese-style cooking, low-key in looks and surprising on the plate.

    Directions ↗

  40. Chef Laura Londoño's tucked-away house: slow-cooked sharing plates where Colombian and Asian flavors meet.

    Directions ↗

  41. A vinyl listening bar in Manila with precise cocktails, at a volume tuned for music and conversation.

    Directions ↗

  42. Boutique yoga studio in Manila offering private classes and an ice bath; intimate and popular with long-stay travelers.

    Directions ↗

  43. A plant-filled house that moves from daytime espresso to evening cocktails, with live jazz on some nights.

    Directions ↗

  44. A multi-brand store of Colombian design: womenswear, accessories and handmade pieces rarely found in malls.

    Directions ↗

  45. Rooftop wellness center offering massages, sauna and yoga; a good way to reset after a day of walking.

    Directions ↗

  46. A B Corp-certified café with understated design, well-executed filter methods and all-day brunch.

    Directions ↗

  47. A tiled, plant-filled atrium, siphon coffee and a Peruvian-accented kitchen: a calm brunch away from the bustle.

    Directions ↗

  48. Green trail along La Presidenta creek with trees, birds and a playground; a natural shortcut between Provenza and El Poblado Avenue.

    Directions ↗

  49. Elcielo-trained chef Yeison Mora cooks with local produce from the Amazon, the Andes and the Pacific.

    Directions ↗

  50. The flagship of Juan Manuel Barrientos, Michelin-starred in the U.S.: a multisensory menu exploring Colombian biodiversity.

    Directions ↗

  51. French-leaning café-bistro serving breakfast all day on a quiet Manila terrace, ideal for an unhurried morning.

    Directions ↗

  52. Time-honored Antioquian cooking with a home-style touch: bandeja paisa, sancocho and slow-cooked beans in a friendly room.

    Directions ↗

  53. A leafy, open-concept mall on the Milla de Oro, with Colombian brands, beauty salons and cafés.

    Directions ↗

  54. The city's flagship mall, with a retractable roof, international labels and Colombian design under one roof.

    Directions ↗

  55. World No. 22 on 50 Best Bars 2026: an elliptical bar, sweeping valley views and a cocktail tasting menu of Colombian biodiversity.

    Directions ↗

  56. Former steel foundry turned contemporary art museum, with a cinema, the Débora Arango collection and terraces in Ciudad del Río.

    Directions ↗

  57. Large food hall in a former warehouse with dozens of global and Colombian kitchens; ideal for indecisive groups.

    Directions ↗

  58. Gothic-style 1930 castle inspired by the Loire Valley, with French gardens; former home of Diego Echavarría, a museum since 1971.

    Directions ↗
